description: Dependency-free .NET 8 APIs for cancellation, task boundaries, bounded parallelism, synchronization, concurrent collections, channels, atomics, and timers.
executionSupportMessage: Compatible with the built-in .NET 10 C# runner; authored against .NET 8.

actionDescriptions.Add: Adds a value, item, header, or contribution to an existing object.
actionDescriptions.Cancel: Requests that cooperative asynchronous or concurrent work stop.
actionDescriptions.Compare: Compares values and reports their ordering or equality relationship.
actionDescriptions.Create: Constructs a new object, resource, or language structure.
actionDescriptions.Get: Retrieves information without intentionally changing the source.
actionDescriptions.Read: Reads text, bytes, messages, or values from a source.
actionDescriptions.Release: Returns or frees a resource previously acquired by the program.
actionDescriptions.Run: Starts work and waits for or observes its outcome.
actionDescriptions.Synchronize: Coordinates access or progress across concurrent operations.
actionDescriptions.Wait: Asynchronously or synchronously pauses until a condition is met.
actionDescriptions.Write: Writes text, bytes, messages, or values to a destination.

objectDescriptions.Cancellation source: A CancellationTokenSource owns a cooperative cancellation signal observed through one or more CancellationToken values.
objectDescriptions.Channel: A Channel<T> is an asynchronous producer-consumer queue with separate reader and writer interfaces and optional backpressure.
objectDescriptions.Concurrent dictionary: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue> provides thread-safe key-value operations, including compound atomic updates.
objectDescriptions.Concurrent queue: ConcurrentQueue<T> is a thread-safe first-in, first-out collection.
objectDescriptions.Lazy value: Lazy<T> defers value construction until first access and then caches the result.
objectDescriptions.Parallel loop: A parallel loop processes several source elements concurrently while respecting configured resource and cancellation limits.
objectDescriptions.Periodic timer: PeriodicTimer provides an asynchronous stream of time-based ticks to a single consumer.
objectDescriptions.Semaphore: SemaphoreSlim controls how many concurrent operations may hold a permit to enter a protected or throttled region.
objectDescriptions.Shared value: A shared value is storage accessed by more than one thread or task and therefore requires atomic or synchronized updates.
objectDescriptions.Task: A Task represents asynchronous work that eventually completes successfully, fails, or is canceled.

commands.name: CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter
commands.description: Schedule a cooperative cancellation request after a delay.
commands.definition: Starts or resets a timer that calls Cancel on the source after the requested duration. Work must observe the associated token for cancellation to take effect.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: The delay before cancellation is requested.

examples.title: Apply a two-second operation budget
examples.explanation: The delay observes the token and throws after the source's timer requests cancellation.

commands.name: CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource
commands.description: Create a token canceled when any source token is canceled.
commands.definition: Creates a new source linked to one or more existing tokens. Its token observes cancellation from any linked source and can also be canceled independently.

examples.title: Combine caller cancellation and a local timeout
examples.explanation: The linked token is canceled by whichever source requests cancellation first.

commands.name: Task.WaitAsync
commands.description: Wait for a task with a timeout or cancellation boundary.
commands.definition: Returns a task that mirrors the original operation when it completes in time, but throws TimeoutException or OperationCanceledException when the selected boundary wins.

examples.title: Bound an asynchronous operation
examples.explanation: The original task completes before the one-second boundary, so its result is returned.

commands.name: Parallel.ForEachAsync
commands.description: Process sequence elements concurrently with bounded parallelism.
commands.definition: Invokes an asynchronous delegate for each source element while respecting ParallelOptions such as MaxDegreeOfParallelism and CancellationToken.

examples.title: Run a bounded set of simulated requests
examples.explanation: At most three delegate bodies run at the same time while every input is eventually processed.

commands.name: SemaphoreSlim.WaitAsync
commands.definition: Waits until the semaphore count is positive, then atomically decrements it. Successful acquisition must be paired with Release, normally in a finally block.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.description: A token that can cancel the wait.

examples.title: Protect a bounded asynchronous section
examples.explanation: The permit is always returned even if the protected operation throws.

commands.name: SemaphoreSlim.Release
commands.description: Return one or more permits to a semaphore.
commands.definition: Increases the semaphore count and allows waiting operations to acquire newly available permits. Releasing beyond the configured maximum throws SemaphoreFullException.

examples.title: Pair release with successful acquisition
examples.explanation: Release occurs exactly once after WaitAsync succeeds.

commands.name: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>.GetOrAdd
commands.description: Get an existing value or atomically publish a generated value.
commands.definition: Returns the value already associated with a key or invokes a factory and attempts to add its result. Under contention, the factory may run more than once even though only one value is stored.

parameters.name: valueFactory
parameters.description: A function that creates a candidate value.

examples.title: Cache a computed label
examples.explanation: The key receives one published value while GetOrAdd returns that value to the caller.

commands.name: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>.AddOrUpdate
commands.description: Atomically add a new value or update the current value.
commands.definition: Uses one factory for a missing key and another for an existing key, retrying when concurrent changes invalidate an attempted update. Factories may execute multiple times.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to add or update.

parameters.name: addValueFactory
parameters.description: A factory for a missing key.

parameters.name: updateValueFactory
parameters.description: A factory receiving the key and current value.

examples.title: Increment a concurrent counter
examples.explanation: The add path starts a key at one, while the update path increments its current value.

commands.name: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>.TryRemove
commands.description: Atomically remove a key and retrieve its value.
commands.definition: Attempts to remove the key-value pair visible at the time of the operation, returning false when the key is absent.

examples.title: Consume a pending work item
examples.explanation: The successful operation removes and returns the same key-value pair atomically.

commands.name: ConcurrentQueue<T>.Enqueue
commands.description: Add an item to a thread-safe FIFO queue.
commands.definition: Places an item at the tail of a ConcurrentQueue<T> without requiring caller-managed locking.

examples.title: Queue work from several tasks
examples.explanation: ConcurrentQueue accepts additions from multiple tasks without an external lock.

commands.name: ConcurrentQueue<T>.TryDequeue
commands.description: Try to remove the oldest item from a thread-safe queue.
commands.definition: Atomically removes and returns the head item when available, or returns false when the queue is empty.

examples.title: Drain queued work
examples.explanation: Each successful call removes the oldest remaining value until the queue is empty.

commands.name: Channel.CreateBounded<T>
commands.description: Create an asynchronous producer-consumer channel with capacity.
commands.definition: Creates a channel whose buffer obeys a maximum capacity and configured full-mode behavior, enabling backpressure between producers and consumers.

examples.title: Create a small backpressure buffer
examples.explanation: The channel holds at most two unread strings, so additional producers wait once it is full.

commands.name: ChannelWriter<T>.WriteAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously write an item to a channel.
commands.definition: Waits for capacity when required, then writes one item unless the channel has completed or cancellation is requested.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.description: A token that can cancel the wait.

examples.title: Publish and complete a channel
examples.explanation: The writer publishes one value and then signals that no later values will arrive.

commands.name: ChannelReader<T>.ReadAllAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously enumerate channel items until completion.
commands.definition: Returns an IAsyncEnumerable<T> that waits for new items and ends after the writer completes and every buffered item has been consumed.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.description: A token that can cancel enumeration.

examples.title: Consume every published value
examples.explanation: Enumeration ends naturally after completion because every buffered item has been read.

commands.name: Interlocked.Increment
commands.definition: Adds one to a variable as a single atomic operation and returns the new value, preventing lost updates between threads.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The int or long storage location to update.

examples.title: Count completions across tasks
examples.explanation: All one hundred increments are retained even though several tasks update the same variable concurrently.

commands.name: Interlocked.Exchange
commands.definition: Stores a new value in a location as one atomic operation and returns the value that was previously present.

examples.title: Publish a one-time state change
examples.explanation: The caller receives the old value while the shared location changes atomically.

commands.name: Interlocked.CompareExchange
commands.description: Atomically replace a value only when it matches an expected value.
commands.definition: Compares a shared location with a comparand and stores a replacement only when equal, returning the location's original value either way.

examples.title: Perform a one-time initialization transition
examples.explanation: Only a caller observing state zero can atomically change it to one.

commands.name: PeriodicTimer.WaitForNextTickAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously wait for the next periodic timer tick.
commands.definition: Waits until the next timer period, cancellation, or disposal. Only one consumer may wait on a PeriodicTimer at a time.

parameters.name: cancellationToken
parameters.description: A token that can cancel the wait.

examples.title: Run three short periodic ticks
examples.explanation: Each iteration waits asynchronously for the next period and stops early if the timer is disposed.

commands.name: Lazy<T>.Value
commands.definition: Returns the cached value, invoking the configured value factory on first access according to the selected thread-safety mode.

examples.title: Initialize expensive data on demand
examples.explanation: The factory runs during the first Value access and its result is reused by the second.
